title: Source first-screen story and dashboard
summary: This iteration turns the first-screen source signal story into four fixed cards and keeps the source metrics dashboard immediately after it as the numeric operating view.

validation_commands: node --test --test-name-pattern "source signal story renders first-screen cards before metrics" tests/unit.test.js

node --test --test-name-pattern "source signal story renders first-screen cards before metrics|source signal story rollup|source-first hero synopsis|source metrics dashboard cards|source-first runtime contract|source status focus|source inventory|source map scan index|source display contract governance" tests/unit.test.js

lessons.lesson: The first source section should be a story surface, not only prose.
lessons.evidence: `source-signal-story` now emits an effective-interact `filterable-cards` section with four fixed cards for the lead source story, visible story titles, included sources, and side-channel or gap states.
lessons.recommended_action: Keep future first-screen source refinements on the fixed card contract so story and metrics remain visually distinct.

lessons.lesson: Metrics should support the source story instead of replacing it.
lessons.evidence: The source-first runtime order still starts with `source-signal-story` and then `source-first-dashboard`; the dashboard card contract and metric definitions remain unchanged.
lessons.recommended_action: Tune metric wording or density only after preserving the story-first ordering contract.

lessons.lesson: Visible source gaps need to stay in the first viewport.
lessons.evidence: The fourth story card exposes updated-not-selected, low-signal, blocked, and skipped/unconfigured source names without hiding them in the later inventory.
lessons.recommended_action: Continue surfacing source gaps before long source maps or inventory sections.

followups.action: Use the next phase to refine source card wording and density after reviewing the next real daily run, without changing source collection or ranking.
